answer: Shared-origin cost ladder makes each new identity from the same network inlet pay a price scaled by recent sibling count. A gale of registrations therefore costs more per identity: with a 10-credit base, the tenth identity pays 90 credits and the hundredth pays 990, so a 100-identity burst costs about 50,000 credits. Prices decay toward base over a 30-day horizon, so slow farming stays cheap while fast batch attacks carry the cost.
